data.body:
Implementation finding: deleting a held-out twin breaks CROSS-FILE references the plan did not enumerate.

The merge itself was clean, but `make verify` failed rc=2 at the import-convention step on
`test_tests_import_convention.py::test_audit_page_modules_collect_under_bare_pytest[test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py]`.
That guard hard-codes the twin's FILENAME in a parametrize list. The earlier 564-test run passed
only because it was scoped to the merged modules; nothing in that scope references a sibling's path.

Sweeping all 39 deleted filenames across the tree (not just the merged files) found 11 references,
of which 4 were runtime-breaking and 6 were stale prose:

RUNTIME (a deleted module path that is actually loaded, collected, or scanned):
1. tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:26 - parametrize list naming the deleted file.
   Fixed: dropped the entry; the base module alone now carries the merged content.
2. tests/unit/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py:35 - builds a pytest NODE ID
   `tests/unit/test_rp04_s4_llm_runtime_heldout.py::{target}` and runs it in a nested pytest.
   Verified all 4 `_TARGETS` names survive the merge UNRENAMED, so only the path changed.
3. tests/unit/test_environ_assert_repr_security.py:38 - `_GUARDED_MODULE` points at the deleted
   file and AST-scans it. Verified `_GUARDED_TEST`
   (`test_both_chains_sign_from_composed_signer_without_env`) exists unrenamed in the base.
4. tests/interfaces/contracts/test_bridge_vocabulary_stale_heldout.py:40 - `_WHOLE_FILE_ALLOWLIST`
   entry permitting retired command spellings. The retired vocabulary moved INTO the base on merge,
   so leaving the stale entry would have failed the base file under the bridge-vocabulary gate.

PROSE (no runtime effect, but now false):
5-8. test_attest_dsse.py, test_attest_registry.py, test_attest_sshsig.py, test_opcert_storage.py -
   module docstrings saying edge cases "live in ``<name>_heldout.py``". Repointed to the held-out
   oracles section now inside the same file.
9. tests/unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py:280 - cross-referenced "the NOTE in
   test_verify_opcert_heldout.py". The explanation survived the merge at test_verify_opcert.py:250-253
   but is NOT labelled "NOTE", so the cross-reference now names it by content.
10. tests/interfaces/facades/test_intercept_registry_cutover_s6_heldout.py:37 - comment pointing at
   a deleted parametrization module.

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE (1): tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py:256. The deleted path
appears inside `_PRE_FIX_VIOLATOR`, a string literal holding the verbatim pre-fix body of a module,
seeded to a temp file so the uniqueness guard is permanently shown to catch the reverted form
(bug 16e1-237d). It is inert text, never collected against the real path; rewriting it would damage
the frozen historical artifact the guard depends on.

Lesson for the remaining twin-merge stories under this epic: the deletion's blast radius is NOT the
merged pair. Sweep every deleted FILENAME across the whole tree, and for each hit decide whether it
is a live path (fix), stale prose (fix), or a frozen literal (leave). Checking only that the merged
modules pass will miss all four runtime breakages.

ruff check tests/ clean; ruff format --check clean; the 5 affected guard modules pass 33/33.
